2607.16938.title: What Do They See? Interpreting Complex Road Scenarios Through the Eyes of Vision-Language-Action Models for Safe and Trustworthy Autonomous Vehicle Learning
2607.16938.paper_summary: End-to-end autonomous driving models are now able to navigate complex road scenarios, mapping raw sensor observations directly to observed paths for open-loop evaluation and often effective driving in closed-loop evaluation. Yet the internal logic of these safety-critical systems remains largely opaque, due to the complexity of traffic scenes. We propose a counterfactual ablation framework called Counterfactual Vision Action Analysis (CVAA) that systematically removes individual detected objects from front-camera images using photorealistic generative inpainting to prepare counterfactual sets to evaluate the difference in the model's response. This isolates the causal effect of each object's presence on the model's planning behaviour. Applied to the Alpamayo 1 trajectory predictor across 210 nuScenes driving scenes, we create a dataset Counter -nuScenes, using which we see that vehicles and pedestrians within the model's 'path' dominate causal influence as expected, while traffic lights, as expected, exert disproportionate effect relative to their image footprint. However, we also find cases where the model responds strongly to objects a human driver would consider irrelevant. This brings forth a deeper question: does the model itself view the scene as a sum of individual objects influencing the outcome, or does it encode an entirely different set of internal features that do not correspond to human-legible scene elements? To further understand this, we compare intermediate representations of original and inpainted image pairs using mechanistic interpretability techniques and examine the effect of the removal through the various model layers. Together, these two stages offer a path from behavioral auditing to representational understanding, creating explainable driving systems and solidifying human-AI trust.
2607.16938.paper_summary_zh: 端對端的自動駕駛模型現在能夠導航複雜的道路場景，將原始傳感器觀察直接映射到觀察到的路徑，以進行開環評估，並在閉環評估中通常實現有效駕駛。然後，由於交通場景的複雜性，這些安全關鍵系統的內部邏輯仍然在很大程度上不透明。我們提出了一個名為反事實視覺行動分析（Counterfactual Vision Action Analysis, CVAA）的反事實消融框架，該框架使用照片真實的生成修補系統系統性地從前置攝像頭圖像中移除個別檢測到的物體，以準備反事實集來評估模型反應的差異。這使得每個物體存在對模型規劃行為的因果影響得以隔離。應用於210個nuScenes駕駛場景中的Alpamayo 1軌跡預測器，我們創建了一個數據集Counter -nuScenes，利用該數據集我們發現模型的“路徑”中的車輛和行人如預期一樣主導因果影響，而交通信號燈則如預期一樣相對於其影像足跡施加不成比例的影響。然而，我們還發現一些情況，其中模型對人類駕駛者認為不相關的物體做出強烈反應。這引出了更深層次的問題：模型本身是否將場景視為影響結果的個別物體的總和，還是它編碼了一組與人類可理解的場景元素不相符的完全不同的內部特徵？為了進一步理解這一點，我們使用機械解釋技術比較原始和修補圖像對的中間表示，並檢查通過各個模型層的移除效果。這兩個階段共同提供了一條從行為審計到表徵理解的道路，創造可解釋的駕駛系統，並鞏固人類與人工智慧之間的信任。
